item.name: ambient-hero
item.summary: Hero composition: ambient canvas (mesh/noise/particles) + TextReveal + MagneticButton (DOM+WebGL, reduced motion -> static, mobile -> T2)

useWhen: Primary landing page hero section requiring an ambient signature moment
Marketing page header with animated headline text reveal and magnetic action buttons
Showcasing a flagship product release with accessible ambient background motion
avoidWhen: Secondary pages or documentation headers where ambient motion distracts from content
Dense data dashboards or form-heavy internal tools
Pages already containing another full-viewport WebGL context above the fold

alternatives.name: noise-field
alternatives.when: When you only need a standalone background canvas without integrated typography or CTAs

alternatives.name: text-reveal
alternatives.when: When you only need headline text reveal animation without ambient background or CTAs

tiers.0: CSS gradient poster background (no WebGL), headline as plain static text, CTAs without magnetic pull (server render, prefers-reduced-motion, Save-Data, no WebGL2)
tiers.1: Poster background; no magnetic pull; the headline animates by word with a 40 ms stagger only if the component mounts on the client (coarse pointer with low-end hints)
tiers.2: WebGL background at DPR <= 1.5; magnetic pull only with a fine pointer; headline animates by word (60 ms stagger) only if the component mounts on the client
tiers.3: WebGL background at DPR <= 2; fine-pointer magnetic pull; headline animates by word only if the component mounts on the client

reducedMotion.description: Renders the static CSS gradient poster background with 0 WebGL canvases and 0 animation frames; headline renders as plain text without splitting or keyframes; buttons remain static

input.pointer: Fine pointer activates magnetic CTA attraction; the pause button stops only the hero's own background (its variant's `paused` prop)
input.touch: Touch devices (coarse pointer) get no magnetic pull; CTA links and the pause button respond to direct tap
input.keyboard: Tab reaches the pause button (when shown), then the CTA links, with default browser focus rings; Enter activates links, Enter or Space activates the pause button

a11y.notes: Single h1 heading (rendered by TextReveal). A scrim built from the host --background token sits between the canvas and the text, so it follows the light or dark theme; it is a contrast aid, not a guarantee, and contrast over the live canvas is not computed at runtime: verify it for your content in both themes. Measured on real pixels over the live canvas in a fresh Next 16 app with shadcn's default tokens (3 variants x light/dark x 1440/390 px, sample copy): every text element at least 10:1. The scrim is strong, so a bolder background needs mesh-gradient (or another background item) directly instead of this composition. Every colour is a host token (--background, --foreground, --primary, --primary-foreground, --muted-foreground, --secondary, --border) with a system-colour fallback. The pause button stops only the hero background; it does not touch the page's other motion or SmoothScroll's scrolling (a global runtime pauseAll() set elsewhere is lifted by Resume). All text stays in the accessibility tree.

props.name: headline
props.effect: Required. Primary document h1 heading rendered by TextReveal by word.

props.name: body
props.effect: Required. Supporting description copy below the headline.

props.name: primaryCta
props.type: AmbientHeroCta = { label: string; href?: string; onClick?: () => void }
props.effect: Required. Primary action link with magnetic pull. Rendered as an <a>; href falls back to '#'.

props.name: variant
props.effect: Selects which ambient background to mount (exactly one WebGL context). Its settings are fixed: mesh speed 0.3, noise speed 0.4 scale 1.8, particles count 2500 speed 0.4.

props.name: background
props.effect: Optional. Custom background slot overriding the ambient generator variant.

props.name: eyebrow
props.effect: Optional. Small pill tag displayed above the headline.

props.name: secondaryCta
props.type: AmbientHeroCta = { label: string; href?: string; onClick?: () => void }
props.effect: Optional. Secondary action link with magnetic pull. Rendered as an <a>; href falls back to '#'.

props.name: showPauseButton
props.effect: Renders a pause/resume button that stops and restarts the hero background only.

props.name: paused
props.effect: Universal pause prop. Freezes the ambient background variant only (not a custom background slot, the headline or the buttons).

props.name: nonce
props.effect: Optional CSP nonce forwarded to the <style> element of the headline reveal.

props.name: className
props.effect: Optional. No default. Additional CSS class names on the root header element. Any other HTML attribute (id, data-*, aria-*, event handlers) is spread on the root element; handlers the item uses itself are composed, not replaced.

props.name: style
props.effect: Optional. No default. Inline styles on the root header element, merged last (consumer wins).

props.name: ref
props.effect: Receives the root <header> element.

mistakes: Do not place a second WebGL item above the fold alongside AmbientHero (violates single signature moment rule).
headline, body and primaryCta are required and there is no default copy: TypeScript fails without them. Pass your own text; never ship the demo's.
The scrim is built from your --background token. It lowers background luminance but is not a contrast guarantee: verify contrast for your content in light and dark.
paused (and the built-in Pause button) reaches the ambient variant only; a custom background slot, the headline reveal and the buttons are not paused by it.
On a server-rendered page the headline is painted as final static text first (TextReveal does not replay on first paint), so do not expect a word-by-word entrance on load.
Reveal styles only apply when <html> has data-motion="ok" (MotionReadyScript in Next, initMotionReady() in Vite).
Under a nonce-based CSP pass nonce: AmbientHero forwards it to the <style> element of its headline reveal.
The pause button pauses the hero background only. Motion elsewhere on the page (other items, Marquee) needs its own pause control or the runtime pauseAll().

The scrim keeps the text readable by muting the background (about 45-85% of --background); the animated background is subtle by design. If the background should be the star, compose your own hero around mesh-gradient, noise-field or particle-field.
verify: Verify that exactly one <h1> element exists in the rendered DOM.
Verify that the pause button toggles motion and has valid aria-label.
Verify that reduced-motion preferences render a static poster with 0 canvases.

items.name: distortion-image
items.title: DistortionImage
items.description: media: WebGL2 hover-displacement image overlay (webgl, client-only, reduced motion -> static image, mobile -> plain image / 0 contexts)

item.name: distortion-image
item.summary: media: WebGL2 hover-displacement image overlay (webgl, client-only, reduced motion -> static image, mobile -> plain image / 0 contexts)

useWhen: Portfolio galleries and editorial features requiring tactile pointer distortion
Product showcases where fine-pointer interaction reveals optical depth
Media elements benefiting from fluid ripple displacement over real images
avoidWhen: Long lists of small thumbnails on mobile where static images are optimal
High-frequency rapid scrolling feeds without user hovering
Images lacking CORS headers when hosted on cross-origin domains

alternatives.name: noise-field
alternatives.when: When a generative ambient canvas background is needed instead of image distortion

tiers.0: Plain image, no WebGL (server render, prefers-reduced-motion, Save-Data, no WebGL2, or frame-guard downgrade)
tiers.1: Plain image (coarse pointer with low-end hints)
tiers.2: WebGL2 displacement overlay at DPR <= 1.5, 0.75 render scale, texture <= 1024px, only when the device reports (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine); coarse-pointer devices at this tier get the plain image
tiers.3: WebGL2 displacement overlay at DPR <= 2.0, full render scale, texture <= 2048px (fine pointer with hover)

reducedMotion.description: Renders the plain static image with no WebGL context and no animation frames.

input.pointer: Fine-pointer hover acquires a context lease and ripples around the cursor. The lease is released about 3 s after the pointer leaves or stops moving, and the render loop keeps running during that idle period (up to about 3.4 s). At most 4 contexts are live per page, shared by all instances; when the budget is full the least recently used idle image gives its slot up.
input.touch: Touch pointers fall back to the plain static image with zero WebGL allocation
input.keyboard: The wrapper is not focusable. For linked images (wrapped in <a> or containing a covering <a>), focus on the link triggers the ripple on fine-pointer devices and draws a two-tone inset focus ring above the canvas, inside the image box so parent overflow:hidden cannot clip it; exactly one tab stop is preserved. Purely decorative images have no keyboard activation. The canvas is aria-hidden

a11y.notes: The underlying HTML img element keeps the full accessible name via alt; the WebGL canvas overlay and focus ring are aria-hidden. A linked image gets exactly one tab stop (the link itself). Keyboard activation is supported whether the image is wrapped in an <a> or contains a covering <a> inside its children.

props.name: alt
props.effect: Required. Accessible alternative text for the image.

props.name: width
props.effect: Optional. No default. Layout width of the wrapper and the img.

props.name: height
props.effect: Optional. No default. Layout height of the wrapper and the img.

props.name: strength

props.name: speed

props.name: maxTier
props.effect: Hard ceiling on the capability tier (0 to 3).

props.name: paused

props.name: crossOrigin
props.effect: Optional. No default. CORS setting for the image. Only set to 'anonymous' when the host server sends Access-Control-Allow-Origin headers. If set on a host without CORS headers, the browser blocks the image entirely. When omitted, images from non-CORS hosts cleanly fall back to static image display without errors.

props.name: fetchPriority
props.effect: Optional. No default. Native fetchpriority attribute forwarded to the underlying img element.

props.name: fetchpriority
props.effect: Optional. No default. Lower-case alias of fetchPriority, used only when fetchPriority is not set.

props.name: loading
props.effect: Native browser image loading attribute.

props.name: decoding
props.effect: Native browser image decoding behavior.

props.name: srcSet
props.effect: Optional. No default. Native srcset. When the browser picks another candidate (resize, DPR change) the new pixels are uploaded to the texture.

props.name: sizes
props.effect: Optional. No default. Native sizes attribute for srcSet.

props.name: imgClassName
props.effect: Class names for the inner img.

props.name: imgStyle
props.effect: Optional. No default. Inline styles merged onto the inner img.

props.name: className
props.effect: Extra classes on the wrapper div. Other HTML div attributes (data-*, aria-*) are passed to the wrapper, not to the img.

props.name: style
props.effect: Optional. No default. Inline styles on the wrapper div, merged after width and height (consumer wins).

props.name: ref
props.effect:
Receives the wrapper
around the (not the itself).

props.name: onPointerEnter
props.effect: Optional. No default. Composed: called first, then the component's own handling. onPointerMove, onPointerLeave, onFocus and onBlur are composed the same way.

props.name: children
props.effect: Optional. No default. Content layered above the image and canvas, for example a caption or a link.

mistakes: Do not set crossOrigin='anonymous' unless the host server actually sends CORS headers (Access-Control-Allow-Origin); setting it on a non-CORS host causes the browser to block the image entirely. Omit it to let DistortionImage cleanly display the static image without errors.
Do not set position: absolute on the underlying img without specifying container dimensions; let the image define layout to avoid CLS.
Do not attempt to animate strength or pointer coordinates manually with requestAnimationFrame; the component handles internal interaction loops.

The wrapper is display: inline-block, set inline, so a `block` class does not override it: pass style={{ display: 'block' }} for block layout, and `w-full` / `aspect-*` classes to size it in a grid. Numeric width and height props set fixed pixels on the wrapper and the .
verify: Confirm the real img element is rendered in server HTML before hydration (CLS <= 0.01).
Confirm that when hovering with a fine pointer, a WebGL context lease is acquired and released after about 3s idle.
Confirm that coarse touch pointers and reduced-motion render the plain image with 0 WebGL contexts.

items.name: magnetic-button
items.title: MagneticButton
items.description: cta: Magnetic spring wrapper for buttons and links with fine-pointer gating (dom, server-safe, reduced motion -> static, mobile -> 0 listeners)

item.name: magnetic-button
item.summary: cta: Magnetic spring wrapper for buttons and links with fine-pointer gating (dom, server-safe, reduced motion -> static, mobile -> 0 listeners)

useWhen: High-priority call-to-action buttons in hero and conversion sections
Interactive icon triggers and primary action links
Header navigation actions seeking tactile physical response
avoidWhen: Dense lists of repeating table buttons or compact toolbar grids
Touch-first mobile interfaces with coarse pointer navigation
Disabled or read-only interactive elements

alternatives.name: text-reveal
alternatives.when: When animating entrance typography rather than interactive hover responses

tiers.0: Static wrapper without pointer handlers or translation (server render, prefers-reduced-motion, Save-Data, or no WebGL2)
tiers.1: Static wrapper without pointer handlers (coarse pointer with low-end hints)
tiers.2: Magnetic pull with the configured strength, only when the device reports (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)
tiers.3: Same behaviour as tier 2: spring physics on the shared frame loop while the pointer is over the wrapper, settling to zero frames

reducedMotion.description: Button retains static position without magnetic cursor tracking.

input.pointer: Cursor attraction with physical spring settling within 0.01px tolerance
input.touch: Zero pointer handlers attached on coarse/touch screens
input.keyboard: Focus snaps the wrapper to its origin immediately and the child's own onFocus still runs; the wrapper uses overflow: visible

a11y.notes: The wrapped button or link keeps its native semantics. The wrapper div uses overflow: visible so it does not clip focus rings, and keyboard focus immediately resets translation to origin.

props.name: children
props.effect: Required. A single interactive element (button or link) wrapped by the magnetic controller.

props.name: pullDistance
props.effect: Maximum pull translation in pixels (replaces deprecated strength).

props.name: paused
props.effect: Universal pause prop. Freezes magnetic displacement calculation.

props.name: tension
props.effect: Spring stiffness coefficient.

props.name: damping
props.effect: Spring velocity damping coefficient.

props.name: className
props.effect: Additional CSS classes applied to the outer wrapper div (the built-in class fb-magnetic-button is kept).

props.name: style
props.effect: Optional. No default. Inline styles on the wrapper div, merged after display: inline-block and position: relative (consumer wins).

props.name: ref
props.effect: Receives the wrapper <div> (not the child button).

props.name: maxTier
props.effect: Hard ceiling on the capability tier.

mistakes: Do not set overflow: hidden on MagneticButton or parent containers, or focus rings will be clipped.
Do not wrap non-interactive static text in MagneticButton; reserve for buttons and action links.

MagneticButton renders a wrapper div (display: inline-block) around the child, so do not place it inside a

or another

Props other than the listed ones (id, data-*, aria-*, onPointerMove, onPointerLeave) are spread on the wrapper <div> (onPointerMove / onPointerLeave are composed with the pull logic). Put aria-* for the control on the child button or link.
ref points at the wrapper <div>, not at the child button. While paused the button stays where it is (it does not spring back until un-paused).
verify: Verify button is immediately clickable and focusable in server HTML.
Verify keyboard tabbing triggers focus ring cleanly without clipped edges.
Verify that on touch screens, zero pointer handlers are registered.

items.name: marquee
items.title: Marquee
items.description: strip: Infinite marquee with inert duplicate, hover/focus pause, and pause button (dom, server-safe, reduced motion -> static, mobile -> animates)

item.name: marquee
item.summary: strip: Infinite marquee with inert duplicate, hover/focus pause, and pause button (dom, server-safe, reduced motion -> static, mobile -> animates)

useWhen: Logo clouds, customer testimonials, and partner strips
Continuous market tickers, tech badges, and announcement banners
Visual social proof ribbons requiring smooth continuous transit
avoidWhen: Critical action buttons or primary call-to-action links that users must click immediately
Dense paragraphs of essential reading material
Pages where multiple moving strips compete for visual attention

alternatives.name: scroll-reveal
alternatives.when: When cards or media should reveal progressively upon scrolling rather than auto-looping

tiers.0: Animation paused and no duplicate copy rendered; the track is a static row, not animated (server render, prefers-reduced-motion, Save-Data, or no WebGL2)
tiers.1: CSS marquee animation; same behaviour as tiers 2 and 3 (speed does not vary by tier)
tiers.2: CSS marquee animation with hover/focus pause, width-based duration calibration and the pause button

reducedMotion.description: The animation does not run: the track is rendered static (not animated), with no duplicate copy and no pause button.

input.pointer: Hovering over the marquee pauses the animation when pauseOnHover is true
input.touch: No touch-specific behaviour; the animation runs on touch devices unless reduced motion is set
input.keyboard: Focus inside the marquee pauses it when pauseOnFocus is true; duplicate items are inert so each item is tabbed once

a11y.notes: The duplicate copy is aria-hidden and inert so screen readers and keyboard users encounter each element once. A built-in pause/play button is shown unless showPauseButton is false or reduced motion is set.

props.name: children
props.effect: Required. Content elements repeated across the strip (rendered twice; avoid fixed ids).

props.name: pixelsPerSecond
props.effect: Transit rate in physical pixels per second (default 40). speed multiplies it. The cycle is never shorter than 5 s.

props.name: speed
props.effect: Unitless multiplier on pixelsPerSecond (1 = as given, 0.5 = half, 2 = double).

props.name: paused
props.effect: Universal pause prop. Freezes ticker transit.

props.name: nonce
props.effect: Optional CSP nonce forwarded to internal scoped <style> element.

props.name: direction
props.effect: Scroll direction of the ticker.

props.name: pauseOnHover
props.effect: Freezes scroll transit while the pointer hovers over the strip.

props.name: pauseOnFocus
props.effect: Freezes scroll transit while any element inside the strip holds keyboard focus.

props.name: showPauseButton
props.effect: Renders a pause/play button (not rendered under reduced motion). Keep it for marquees that run longer than 5 s.

props.name: gap
props.effect: Spacing between items (a number is treated as px).

props.name: className
props.effect: CSS classes applied to the outer container (the built-in class fb-marquee is kept).

props.name: style
props.effect: Optional. No default. Inline styles on the outer container, merged last (consumer wins).

props.name: ref
props.effect: Receives the root <div>.

props.name: maxTier
props.effect: Hard ceiling on the capability tier.

mistakes: Do not remove the inert attribute from duplicate tracks or screen readers will double-read every item.
Do not hide the pause control if the marquee runs continuously for more than 5 seconds (WCAG 2.2.2).
The animation only runs when <html> has data-motion="ok" (MotionReadyScript in Next, initMotionReady() in Vite); without it the strip is static.
Children are rendered twice, so do not give them fixed id attributes. Other props (id, data-*, aria-*, handlers) are spread on the root <div>.
verify: Verify screen reader encounters each badge/item exactly once.
Verify hovering or focusing an item pauses animation transit.
Verify reduced motion stops the animation and renders a static row without a duplicate copy or pause button.
Confirm Pause then Play resumes the animation while the pointer or keyboard focus is still on the button.

item.name: mesh-gradient
item.summary: background: multi-color organic mesh gradient via WebGL2 (webgl2, client-only, reduced motion -> static poster, DPR <= 1.5 on mobile/Tier 2)

useWhen: Hero sections requiring rich, fluid multi-color ambient backgrounds
Telemetry or premium landing surfaces needing organic color transitions
Sections requiring soft chromatic fields with zero server hydration shift
avoidWhen: Dense text sections where text contrast over the gradient has not been verified
Surfaces already running another full-screen WebGL shader in the same viewport
Devices with battery-saver or forced reduced motion enabled

alternatives.name: noise-field
alternatives.when: When monochromatic procedural simplex flow lines are desired

alternatives.name: particle-field
alternatives.when: When discrete kinematic points and pointer repulsion are preferred

tiers.0: CSS multi-radial gradient poster only, no WebGL (server render, prefers-reduced-motion, Save-Data, no WebGL2, or frame-guard downgrade)
tiers.1: CSS multi-radial gradient poster only (coarse pointer with low-end hints: deviceMemory <= 2 or <= 4 cores)
tiers.2: WebGL2 at DPR <= 1.5, 0.75 render scale, 2 octaves (coarse pointer without low-end hints, or fine pointer with low-end hints or viewport < 480px)
tiers.3: WebGL2 at DPR <= 2.0, full render scale, 4 octaves (fine pointer with hover, no low-end hints)

reducedMotion.description: Renders the static CSS gradient poster with no WebGL context and no animation frames (Decision 14 D-A). Under prefers-reduced-motion the runtime tier is 0, so WebGL does not start.

input.touch: None; no touch or pointer listeners. Coarse pointers with low-end hints get the tier 1 poster; other coarse-pointer devices run WebGL at tier 2.
input.keyboard: None; the component has no interactive elements. Poster, scrim and canvas layers are aria-hidden; children keep their own semantics.

a11y.notes: The poster, scrim and canvas layers are aria-hidden; the root element and children are not. There is no built-in pause button: pause with the paused prop or the runtime pauseAll()/resumeAll(). The optional scrim lowers background luminance behind children but contrast is not computed; verify text contrast for your colours.

props.name: colors
props.effect: CSS colours resolved from host tokens. Only the first four are used (extra entries are ignored); missing entries reuse earlier ones. The first colour is the background.

props.name: speed
props.effect: Wave drift speed multiplier.

props.name: distortion
props.effect: Amplitude of organic noise distortion.

props.name: swirl
props.effect: Vortex swirl strength in the gradient field.

props.name: grainMixer
props.effect: Subtle analog grain distortion strength.

props.name: grainOverlay
props.effect: Post-processing fine film grain overlay intensity.

props.name: scrim
props.effect: Renders a radial scrim of the first colour (20% centre to 80% edge opacity) over the canvas to lower background luminance behind children. Does not guarantee text contrast; verify for your colours.

props.name: paused
props.effect: Freezes this instance's shader animation loop. The global pauseAll() also stops it.

props.name: maxTier
props.effect: Upper bound on the capability tier (0 to 3); the tier is the minimum of this and the runtime tier.

props.name: reducedMotion
props.effect: Optional. No default (follows prefers-reduced-motion). true forces the static poster. false only skips the prop-level check: under prefers-reduced-motion the runtime tier is still 0, so WebGL still does not start. Leave unset.

props.name: className
props.effect: Extra classes on the root div (the built-in class fb-mesh-gradient is kept).

props.name: style
props.effect: Optional. No default. Inline styles on the root div, merged after the built-in layout and background colour (consumer wins).

props.name: ref
props.effect: Receives the root <div> that holds the poster and the canvas.

props.name: children
props.effect: Optional. No default. Content layered above the poster, canvas and scrim.

mistakes: Do not combine multiple MeshGradient instances in the same viewport.

scrim defaults to false. Turn it on behind text, but it only lowers background luminance and does not guarantee 4.5:1 contrast: verify contrast for your colours and use host foreground tokens for text.
Do not set reducedMotion={false} to try to force WebGL; it does not override the user's preference (the runtime tier stays 0 under prefers-reduced-motion).
Never call requestAnimationFrame directly to animate the mesh.
verify: Confirm the static CSS multi-radial gradient poster renders in server HTML (CLS <= 0.01).
Confirm that when prefers-reduced-motion is active, the static poster renders with zero WebGL contexts allocated and zero rAF cycles.
Confirm context lease is released when scrolled out of view.

Do not set reducedMotion={false} to try to force WebGL; it does not override the user's preference (the runtime tier stays 0 under prefers-reduced-motion).
Do not combine multiple NoiseField components in the same viewport; follow the one signature moment principle.
The root element uses Tailwind utility classes (relative, w-full, h-full, min-h-[300px], overflow-hidden); install it in a Tailwind project.
Never call requestAnimationFrame directly to animate NoiseField props; let the runtime handle the loop.

Confirm that when prefers-reduced-motion is active, the static poster renders with zero WebGL contexts allocated and zero rAF cycles.
Confirm context lease is properly released when scrolled out of view.

item.name: particle-field
item.summary: background: WebGL2 vertex-shader particle drift with pointer repel (webgl2, client-only, reduced motion -> poster, mobile -> tier 2 / tier 1 poster)

useWhen: Hero sections requiring discrete starry or kinetic depth points
Telemetry or scientific landing pages needing particle drift and fine pointer interaction
Surfaces seeking subtle stellar motion with constant GPU cost
avoidWhen: Dense text sections where text contrast over the particles has not been verified
Pages already running a continuous full-screen shader
Low-power mobile devices where the static dot pattern is preferred

alternatives.name: noise-field
alternatives.when: When continuous organic liquid waves are preferred over discrete points

alternatives.name: mesh-gradient
alternatives.when: When soft blurred color transitions are preferred

tiers.0: CSS dot-pattern poster only, no WebGL (server render, prefers-reduced-motion, Save-Data, no WebGL2, or frame-guard downgrade)
tiers.1: CSS dot-pattern poster only (coarse pointer with low-end hints: deviceMemory <= 2 or <= 4 cores)
tiers.2: WebGL2 at DPR <= 1.5 with 35% of `count` particles (coarse pointer without low-end hints, or fine pointer with low-end hints or viewport < 480px)
tiers.3: WebGL2 at DPR <= 2.0 with `count` particles, up to 4,000 (fine pointer with hover, no low-end hints)

reducedMotion.description: Renders the static CSS dot-pattern poster with no WebGL context and no animation frames. Under prefers-reduced-motion the runtime tier is 0, so WebGL does not start.

input.pointer: Pointer repulsion within a 140px radius, only when interactive is true and the device reports pointer: fine (window pointermove listener, mouse and pen only)
input.touch: No pointer listeners are attached when the device does not report pointer: fine. Coarse pointers with low-end hints get the tier 1 poster; other coarse-pointer devices run the drift at tier 2.
input.keyboard: None; the component has no interactive elements. Poster, scrim and canvas layers are aria-hidden; children keep their own semantics.

a11y.notes: The poster, scrim and canvas layers are aria-hidden; the root element and children are not. Particle twinkle runs at about 0.3 Hz (sin(phase + time * 1.8) in the vertex shader), well below 3 flashes per second. There is no built-in pause button: pause with the paused prop or the runtime pauseAll()/resumeAll(). The optional scrim lowers background luminance but contrast is not computed; verify text contrast for your colours.

props.name: color
props.effect: Particle CSS colour, resolved from CSS variables or theme tokens and also used for the dot-pattern poster.

props.name: speed
props.effect: Kinematic drift rate multiplier.

props.name: count
props.effect: Target particle count on Tier 3 (clamped to 4,000). Tier 2 renders 35% of it.

props.name: interactive
props.effect: Enables pointer repulsion; only active when the device reports pointer: fine.

props.name: scrim
props.effect: Renders a vertical gradient of the host --background token (40% to 75% opacity) over the canvas to lower background luminance behind children. Does not guarantee text contrast; verify for your colours.

props.name: paused
props.effect: Freezes this instance's particle loop. The global pauseAll() also stops it.

props.name: maxTier
props.effect: Upper bound on the capability tier (0 to 3); the tier is the minimum of this and the runtime tier.

props.name: reducedMotion
props.effect: Optional. No default (follows prefers-reduced-motion). true forces the static poster. false only skips the prop-level check: under prefers-reduced-motion the runtime tier is still 0, so WebGL still does not start. Leave unset.

props.name: className
props.effect: Extra classes on the root div (the built-in class fb-particle-field is kept).

props.name: style
props.effect: Optional. No default. Inline styles on the root div, merged after the built-in layout and background (consumer wins).

props.name: ref
props.effect: Receives the root <div> that holds the poster and the canvas.

props.name: children
props.effect: Optional. No default. Content layered above the poster, canvas and scrim.

mistakes: Do not attach your own window mouse listeners for repulsion; ParticleField already adds one window pointermove listener, only on devices that report pointer: fine.
Do not combine multiple ParticleField instances in the same viewport.
scrim defaults to false. It only lowers background luminance and does not guarantee 4.5:1 contrast: verify contrast for your colours and use host foreground tokens for text.
Do not set reducedMotion={false} to try to force WebGL; it does not override the user's preference (the runtime tier stays 0 under prefers-reduced-motion).
Never call requestAnimationFrame directly to animate particles.
verify: Confirm the static CSS dot-pattern poster renders in server HTML (CLS <= 0.01).
Confirm that when prefers-reduced-motion is active, the static poster renders with zero WebGL contexts allocated and zero rAF cycles.
Confirm context lease is released when scrolled out of view.

item.name: scroll-reveal
item.summary: media: Scroll-driven entrance (CSS view() timeline, IntersectionObserver fallback) (dom, server-safe, reduced motion -> static, low-end mobile -> 12px)

useWhen: Feature cards, images, and marketing content blocks entering the viewport
Staggered grid items revealing progressively during downward scroll
Sections where scroll-triggered visibility enhances progressive narrative
avoidWhen: Above-the-fold hero elements that must paint immediately for LCP
Sticky navigation bars or persistent floating controls
Dense data tables and interactive form fields

alternatives.name: text-reveal
alternatives.when: When revealing headline text tokens rather than containers or media elements

tiers.0: Content fully visible and static, no reveal classes (server render, prefers-reduced-motion, Save-Data, or no WebGL2)
tiers.1: Reveal with the travel distance capped at 12px (coarse pointer with low-end hints)
tiers.2: Reveal with the configured travel distance (24px by default)
tiers.3: Same as tier 2. At every animated tier, browsers that support animation-timeline use the scroll-linked CSS animation; others use the IntersectionObserver fallback. The observer hook is mounted in both cases.

reducedMotion.description: Content is rendered in its final visible state without transition delays or scroll triggers.

input.pointer: Scroll-linked entrance as the container enters the viewport. Where animation-timeline: view() is supported the animation is scroll-linked and reverses when scrolling back up.
input.touch: Same scroll trigger; the travel distance is capped at 12px only on tier 1 and tier 0 devices
input.keyboard: Focus-within guard forces element visible immediately when tabbed into

a11y.notes: Focus guard forces any element containing active focus visible immediately, preventing keyboard traps during scroll. Hidden-before-reveal styles exist only under html[data-motion="ok"]; server HTML and reduced-motion users see the content visible.

props.name: children
props.effect: Required. Content elements wrapped and revealed on scroll.

props.name: as
props.effect: HTML tag rendered as root container.

props.name: animation
props.effect: Visual entrance variant.

props.name: distance
props.effect: Vertical travel distance in pixels (half of it for scale-up); capped at 12 when the tier is 1 or lower.

props.name: duration
props.effect: Transition duration in ms. Applies only to the IntersectionObserver fallback; the native view-timeline animation is scroll-linked and ignores it.

props.name: once
props.effect: In the IntersectionObserver fallback, true keeps the content revealed after the first entry. The native view-timeline path is scroll-linked and reverses when scrolling back up regardless of this prop.

props.name: className
props.effect: Extra classes on the root element (the built-in class fb-scroll-reveal is kept).

props.name: style
props.effect: Optional. No default. Inline styles on the root element, merged after display: block and position: relative (consumer wins).

props.name: ref
props.effect: Receives the root element chosen by `as`.

props.name: maxTier
props.effect: Hard ceiling on the capability tier.

props.name: paused
props.effect: Universal pause prop. Forces the content visible and still. Where the browser supports CSS scroll-driven animation the reveal is driven by the scroll position and this prop has no effect.

props.name: nonce
props.effect: Optional CSP nonce forwarded to the internal scoped <style> element (one is rendered per instance).

mistakes: Do not use ScrollReveal on above-the-fold hero elements; hero text should be visible immediately for LCP.
Do not nest ScrollReveal components inside each other; keep entrance containers flat.
The reveal only runs when <html> has data-motion="ok" (MotionReadyScript in Next, initMotionReady() in Vite); without it the content is static.
Other props (id, data-*, aria-*, handlers) are spread on the root element.
verify: Verify content is visible in server HTML without JavaScript execution.
Verify tabbing into hidden cards forces them visible immediately via focus guard.
Verify reduced motion renders final visible content with zero animation delays.

item.name: scroll-showcase
item.summary: Scroll composition: StickyScrollStory + ScrollReveal + optional Marquee; all copy comes from props (DOM, reduced motion -> static/opacity, mobile -> stacked)

useWhen: Product feature narrative requiring sticky step progression and reveal on scroll
Product or engineering deep-dive with step-by-step media and an optional metrics grid
Multi-section storytelling with accessible scroll-driven reveals
avoidWhen: Short single-screen pages without scroll depth
Mobile web apps requiring dense vertical list views
Documentation sites where uninterrupted linear reading is essential

alternatives.name: sticky-scroll-story
alternatives.when: When you only need the sticky step column without accompanying feature grids or marquee

alternatives.name: scroll-reveal
alternatives.when: When you only need basic reveal-on-scroll animations for individual cards

tiers.0: Not gated by tier: layout stacks at viewport width 768px and below; ScrollReveal content is static; Marquee is paused with no duplicate copy
tiers.1: ScrollReveal travel capped at 12px; Marquee still animates; layout depends on viewport width, not tier
tiers.2: Sticky story with CSS crossfades, scroll-linked or IntersectionObserver reveals, animated marquee

reducedMotion.description: StickyScrollStory swaps media instantly (no transition, no translation); ScrollReveal elements are immediately visible; Marquee stops animating and renders a static row (no duplicate copy, no pause button)

input.pointer: Hovering the marquee pauses it; the sticky story is driven by scroll position
input.touch: At viewport width 768px and below the story is stacked without sticky positioning
input.keyboard: DOM order matches visual order; the only added focusable element is the marquee pause button, and focus inside the marquee pauses it

a11y.notes: Sections are named through aria-labelledby (the headline, and the specs heading when you pass one) or aria-label (marqueeLabel when you pass one); ids are generated per instance with useId, so two sections on one page never clash. Heading levels run h2 (headline), h2 (each step title, from StickyScrollStory), h3 (specsHeading), h4 (spec labels): place the section under an h1 and check the outline for your page. media.alt applies only to media.type 'image'. Every colour is a host token (--background, --foreground, --primary, --muted-foreground, --card, --border) with a system-colour fallback; contrast follows your theme: measured on real pixels in a fresh Next 16 app with shadcn's default tokens (sample content, light and dark, 1440 and 390 px) every text element was at least 4.7:1 (light) and 6.9:1 (dark); verify your own content.

props.name: headline
props.effect: Required. Primary section headline rendered as an h2.

props.name: description
props.effect: Required. Section narrative description below the headline.

props.name: steps
props.effect: Required. Narrative steps for StickyScrollStory ({ id, title, description, badge?, media }).

props.name: eyebrow
props.effect: Optional. Eyebrow badge above the headline.

props.name: specs
props.effect: Optional. Specifications / highlights grid items ({ metric, label, detail }).

props.name: specsHeading
props.effect: Optional. Heading above the specifications grid. Nothing is rendered when omitted.

props.name: specsEyebrow
props.effect: Optional. Small label above the specifications heading. Nothing is rendered when omitted.

props.name: showMarquee
props.effect: Shows the marquee ticker when marqueeItems is non-empty.

props.name: marqueeItems
props.effect: Optional. Array of items to display in the marquee ticker.

props.name: marqueeLabel
props.effect: Optional. Label above the marquee ticker, also its accessible name. Nothing is rendered when omitted.

props.name: smoothScroll
props.effect: Wraps the composition in the SmoothScroll provider (off by default).

props.name: paused
props.effect: Universal pause prop. Passed to the reveals, the story, the marquee and SmoothScroll (the reveals only react when the browser lacks CSS scroll-driven animation).

props.name: nonce
props.effect: Optional CSP nonce forwarded to the <style> element of every item the section renders.

props.name: className
props.effect: Optional. No default. Additional CSS class names on the root container. Any other HTML attribute (id, data-*, aria-*, event handlers) is spread on the root element; handlers the item uses itself are composed, not replaced.

props.name: style
props.effect: Optional. No default. Inline styles on the root container, merged last (consumer wins).

props.name: ref
props.effect: Receives the root <div>.

mistakes: headline, description and steps are required and the component contains no copy of its own: nothing is rendered for specsHeading, specsEyebrow or marqueeLabel unless you pass them.
StickyScrollStory renders each step's media.content twice (a sticky column and a stacked mobile copy), so do not put ids inside it.
Do not enable smoothScroll on dashboards or documentation pages, and never when another SmoothScroll is mounted (a second one warns and does nothing).
Do not place multiple sticky scroll sections immediately adjacent to each other without spacing.
Under a nonce-based CSP pass nonce: it is forwarded to every <style> the section renders.
Reveal and marquee animations only run when <html> has data-motion="ok" (MotionReadyScript in Next, initMotionReady() in Vite).
verify: Verify that the step sequence is fully accessible in DOM reading order.
Verify that mobile viewports switch to stacked mode without sticky jumping.
Verify that reduced-motion preferences stop the marquee animation and reveals remain static.

items.title: SmoothScroll
items.description: page-provider: Lenis provider stepped strictly via useFrame with autoRaf false (dom, server-safe, singleton, reduced motion -> off, mobile -> off)

item.name: smooth-scroll
item.summary: page-provider: Lenis provider stepped strictly via useFrame with autoRaf false (dom, server-safe, singleton, reduced motion -> off, mobile -> off)

useWhen: Marketing landing pages requiring unified cinematic scroll feel
Editorial feature stories paired with sticky scroll narratives
Desktop viewports with fine pointers and high-refresh displays
avoidWhen: Dashboards and data-dense productivity software
Documentation sites and code-heavy portals
Forms-heavy pages and modal-only checkout flows
Touchscreens and mobile devices (automatically disabled on coarse pointers)

alternatives.name: native-scroll
alternatives.when: When standard browser compositor scrolling is sufficient without kinetic interpolation

tiers.0: Not gated by tier. Smooth scrolling runs unless reduced motion, enabled={false} or a coarse pointer disables it; Save-Data and no-WebGL2 (tier 0) do not disable it
tiers.1: Coarse pointer: disabled, native touch momentum scrolling preserved
tiers.2: Coarse pointer: disabled. On a fine or absent pointer (low-end hints or viewport < 480px) smooth scrolling runs, stepped via useFrame
tiers.3: Smooth scrolling runs (fine pointer with hover), stepped via useFrame; same behaviour as tier 2 on fine pointers

reducedMotion.description: Disabled completely; 100% native platform momentum scrolling.

input.pointer: Wheel input is interpolated by Lenis (smoothWheel) unless the pointer is coarse, reduced motion is set, or enabled is false
input.touch: Native touch momentum scrolling is preserved; Lenis is inactive on coarse pointers
input.keyboard: Keys (Space, PageUp, PageDown, arrows, Home, End) scroll natively; Lenis does not intercept them and a keydown only wakes the shared frame loop

a11y.notes: Native keyboard scrolling is preserved. When reduced motion is preferred, smooth scrolling is turned off completely, delegating all scroll behavior to the native platform compositor.

props.name: children
props.effect: Optional. No default. Child components wrapped inside the provider (rendered in a display: contents div).

props.name: duration
props.effect: Scroll easing duration in milliseconds (e.g. 1200 means 1.2 seconds).

props.name: paused
props.effect: Universal pause prop. Freezes kinetic smooth scrolling.

props.name: easing
props.effect: Easing function (default is a module-level function). Read through a ref, so an inline function does not recreate Lenis.

props.name: orientation
props.effect: Primary scroll orientation.

props.name: gestureOrientation
props.effect: Gesture direction Lenis listens to.

props.name: smoothWheel
props.effect: Whether to interpolate mouse wheel deltas.

props.name: touchMultiplier
props.effect: Lenis touch multiplier (touch scrolling is not smoothed on coarse pointers because SmoothScroll is disabled there).

props.name: infinite
props.effect: Lenis infinite scroll option.

props.name: enabled
props.effect: Master toggle to enable or disable smooth scrolling.

props.name: onScroll
props.effect: Called with the Lenis scroll event (not the DOM scroll event, even though the root is a <div>).

props.name: prevent
props.effect: Optional. No default. Predicate to bypass smooth scrolling for specific DOM nodes. Nested scrollers (allowNestedScroll) and [role="dialog"], [aria-modal="true"], dialog[open], [data-lenis-prevent] are always bypassed.

props.name: ref
props.effect: Receives the root <div>, which is display: contents, so its bounding box is empty (use it for data attributes, not geometry).

mistakes: Do not mount multiple SmoothScroll instances; SmoothScroll is a singleton provider (a second mount warns and does nothing).
Do not import Lenis directly or create separate requestAnimationFrame loops.
Do not use on dashboards, forms-heavy pages, or data-dense web applications.
The registry installs lenis@1.3.26 and consumers accept lenis@^1.3.26; to pin exactly run: npm install --save-exact lenis@1.3.26 (or the equivalent for your package manager).

SmoothScroll is stepped by the shared useFrame loop. While the runtime pauseAll() is active (the runtime global pause; AmbientHero's own pause button no longer triggers it) that loop, and therefore SmoothScroll's stepping, is stopped; verify wheel scrolling on pages that combine them.
duration is in milliseconds (1200 = 1.2 s). A seconds value such as 1.2 now means 1.2 ms and the scroll looks instant.
verify: Verify keyboard navigation (Space, PageUp/Down, Arrows) works identically to native scrolling.
Verify hash anchors (#section-id) jump smoothly without layout offsets.
Verify reduced motion disables Lenis and returns 100% control to the platform.

items.name: sticky-scroll-story

item.name: sticky-scroll-story
item.summary: scroll-section: Sticky media column with scrolling steps (dom, server-safe, CLS <= 0.01, reduced motion -> opacity-only (instant swap), mobile -> stacked)

useWhen: Editorial feature walk-throughs with accompanying media illustrations
Product showcase stories highlighting sequential capabilities
Multi-step walkthroughs where media changes as user reads through text
avoidWhen: Short single-paragraph descriptions without multi-step progression
Galleries where media should scroll freely rather than remain sticky
Dense data tables and forms

alternatives.name: scroll-reveal
alternatives.when: When revealing standalone cards or sections without pinned media

tiers.0: Not gated by tier: sticky two-column layout above 768px, stacked at 768px and below (same at every tier)
tiers.1: Same as tier 0; layout depends on viewport width, not tier
tiers.2: Same as tier 0; layout depends on viewport width, not tier
tiers.3: Same as tier 0; layout depends on viewport width, not tier

reducedMotion.description: Media swaps are instant (inactive media is hidden with opacity 0 and transitions are disabled, so there is no fade); no translation or parallax. Server HTML keeps all media visible.

input.pointer: None; active step is driven solely by scroll position (IntersectionObserver)
input.touch: Stacked layout at viewport width 768px and below, with media shown inline under each step
input.keyboard: Native focus order and keyboard scrolling; the component adds no focusable elements

a11y.notes: DOM order matches reading order. The active step has aria-current='step'. Image media (media.type 'image') gets alt from media.alt, falling back to the step title. Custom media (media.content) gets no alt: supply accessible text inside the content yourself. Each step's media is rendered twice (sticky column and inline mobile copy); only one is visible at a time.

props.name: steps
props.effect: Required. Array of { id: string; title: string; description: string; badge?: string; media: { type?: "image" | "custom"; src?: string; alt?: string; content?: React.ReactNode } }.

props.name: mediaPosition
props.effect: Alignment of the sticky media column relative to the text narrative.

props.name: onStepChange
props.effect: Optional. No default. Called with the step id when a step becomes active.

props.name: paused
props.effect: Universal pause prop. Stops tracking the scrolled step: the active step stays where it is.

props.name: nonce
props.effect: Optional CSP nonce forwarded to the internal scoped <style> element.

props.name: className
props.effect: Optional CSS class names to apply to root container.

props.name: style
props.effect: Optional. No default. Inline styles for the root container.

props.name: ref
props.effect: Receives the root <div>.

mistakes: Do not attach window scroll listeners to calculate sticky step progress; StickyScrollStory uses IntersectionObserver.
Do not invert DOM order; reading order must match step sequence for assistive technology.
media.alt is only used when media.type is 'image'; for custom media put accessible text inside media.content.
The inactive-media hiding only applies under html[data-motion="ok"] (MotionReadyScript in Next, initMotionReady() in Vite) or after hydration with reduced motion.
Each step's media.content is rendered twice (sticky column and stacked mobile copy): no ids inside it. Step titles are h2 elements; put your section heading above them accordingly.
verify: Verify mobile layout (<= 768px) cleanly stacks steps and media without sticky jumps.
Verify aria-current='step' updates as steps scroll through the viewport center.
Verify CLS <= 0.01 during rapid scrolling.

item.name: text-reveal
item.summary: headline: word/line/char text reveal (dom, server-safe, SSR text stays static, reduced motion -> static, low-end mobile -> 40 ms stagger)

avoidWhen: Long paragraphs or running prose (> 2 lines of body text)

alternatives.name: scroll-reveal
alternatives.when: When revealing whole blocks, cards, or media rather than individual text tokens

tiers.0: Plain static text, no splitting (server render, prefers-reduced-motion, Save-Data, or no WebGL2)
tiers.1: Animated reveal with the stagger capped at 40 ms (coarse pointer with low-end hints)
tiers.2: Animated reveal with the configured stagger (60 ms by default)

props.name: children
props.effect: Required. Plain text string to split and reveal (not JSX).

props.name: as
props.effect: HTML tag to render as root container.

props.name: by
props.effect: Token granularity for entrance stagger.

props.name: delay
props.effect: Initial delay in ms before animation begins.

props.name: stagger
props.effect: Delay in ms between subsequent token animations. Capped at 40 ms when the tier is 1 or lower.

props.name: duration
props.effect: Duration in ms for each token entrance.

props.name: className
props.effect: Extra classes on the root element (the built-in class fb-text-reveal is kept).

props.name: style
props.effect: Optional. No default. Inline styles on the root element, merged after position: relative and display: block (consumer wins).

props.name: ref
props.effect: Receives the root element chosen by `as` (it also contains the scoped <style> and a screen-reader copy of the text).

props.name: maxTier
props.effect: Hard ceiling on the capability tier.

props.name: replayKey
props.effect: Optional. No default. When set (or changed), the entrance animation plays after hydration even for a server-rendered instance.

props.name: paused
props.effect: Universal pause prop. Renders plain static text instead of the animated tokens; un-pausing replays the reveal from the start (it does not freeze mid-animation).

props.name: nonce
props.effect: Optional CSP nonce forwarded to the internal scoped <style> element.

mistakes: Do not pass complex React elements or JSX as children; TextReveal expects a text string to tokenize.
Do not hide text with opacity: 0 before hydration; the component handles static visibility safely.
A server-rendered TextReveal is painted as final static text and does not animate unless replayKey is set; do not expect a reveal on a Next.js server-rendered hero without it.
Other props (data-*, aria-*, handlers) are spread on the root element; do not pass your own id (the component uses its own to detect a server render).
The reveal styles apply only when <html> has data-motion="ok" (MotionReadyScript in Next, initMotionReady() in Vite).
verify: Verify full headline text is present in server HTML before JavaScript executes.
Verify screen reader reads text as a single coherent sentence without letter-by-letter pauses.
Verify reduced motion produces immediate static text with zero rAF cycles.
